connections.why: The particle model explains why substances change state
Diffusion and dissolving are explained by moving particles
The atomic model defines what atoms, elements and compounds are
Formulae record which atoms make up an element or compound
Equations use formulae to show how atoms are rearranged
Atoms are only rearranged, so mass is conserved in a reaction
Combustion, decomposition and displacement are kinds of rearrangement
Neutralisation is a reaction type producing salts and water
Chemical reactions release or absorb energy as bonds rearrange
Changing state involves energy transfer to or from particles
Elements are arranged in the table by their properties
Position in the table predicts how an element will react
Reactivity trends underpin the order of the reactivity series
Displacement reactions follow the reactivity series
A pure substance is a single element or compound
Separation techniques isolate pure substances from mixtures
The Earth's materials are the finite resources we recycle
Combustion of fuels releases the carbon dioxide affecting climate
